In [[number theory]], specifically the study of [[modular forms]], a '''Maass–Shimura operator''' is an operator which maps modular forms to [[almost holomorphic modular form]]s.

== Definition ==
The Maass–Shimura operator on (almost holomorphic) modular forms of weight <math>k</math> is defined by
<math display="block">\delta_kf(z):=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\left(\frac{k}{2iy}+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right)f(z)</math>
where <math>y</math> is the [[imaginary part]] of <math>z</math>.

One may similarly define Maass–Shimura operators of higher orders, where 
<math display="block">\begin{aligned}\delta_k^{(n)}&:=\delta_{k+2n-2}\delta_{k+2n-4}\cdots\delta_{k+2}\delta_k\\&=\frac{1}{(2\pi i)^n}\left(\frac{k+2n-2}{2iy}+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right)\left(\frac{k+2n-4}{2iy}+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right)\cdots\left(\frac{k+2}{2iy}+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right)\left(\frac{k}{2iy}+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\right),\end{aligned}</math>
and <math>\delta_k^{(0)}</math> is taken to be identity.

== Properties ==
Maass–Shimura operators raise the weight of a function's modularity by 2. If <math>f</math> is modular of weight <math>k</math> with respect to a [[congruence subgroup]] <math>\varGamma\subseteq\mathrm{SL}_2(\Z)</math>, then <math>\delta_kf</math> is modular with weight <math>k+2</math>:<ref name="Shimura">{{Cite journal |last=Shimura |first=Goro |authorlink=Goro Shimura |year=1975 |title=On some arithmetic properties of modular forms of one and several variables |journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |volume=102 |pages=491–515 |doi=10.2307/1971041}}</ref>
<math display="block">(\delta_kf)(\gamma z)=(\delta_kf(z))(cz+d)^{k+2}\quad\text{for any }\gamma=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in\varGamma.</math>
However, <math>\delta_kf</math> is not a modular form due to the introduction of a non-holomorphic part.

Maass–Shimura operators follow a [[product rule]]: for almost holomorphic modular forms <math>f</math> and <math>g</math> with respective weights <math>k</math> and <math>\ell</math> (from which it is seen that <math>fg</math> is modular with weight <math>k+\ell</math>), one has
<math display="block">\delta_{k+\ell}(fg)=(\delta_kf)g+f(\delta_\ell g).</math>

Using [[Mathematical induction|induction]], it is seen that the iterated Maass–Shimura operator satisfies the identity
<math display="block">\delta_k^{(n)}=\sum_{r=0}^n(-1)^{n-r}\binom{n}{r}\frac{(k+r)_{n-r}}{(4\pi y)^{n-r}}\frac{1}{(2\pi i)^r}\frac{\partial^r}{\partial z^r}</math>
where <math>(a)_m=\Gamma(a+m)/\Gamma(a)</math> is a [[Falling and rising factorials|Pochhammer symbol for a rising factorial]].<ref name="Zagier">{{cite book |last=Zagier |first=Don |authorlink=Don Zagier |chapter=Elliptic Modular Forms and Their Applications |title=The 1-2-3 of Modular Forms |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |year=2008}}</ref>

Lanphier showed a relation between the Maass–Shimura and [[Rankin–Cohen bracket]] operators:<ref name="Lanphier">{{Cite journal |last=Lanphier |first=Dominic |year=2008 |title=Combinatorics of Maass–Shimura operators |journal=[[Journal of Number Theory]] |volume=128 |issue=8 |pages=2467–2487 |doi=10.1016/j.jnt.2007.10.010 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
<math display="block">(\delta_k^{(n)}f(z))g(z)=\sum_{j=0}^n\frac{(-1)^j\binom{n}{j}\binom{k+n-1}{n-j}}{\binom{k+\ell+2j-2}{j}\binom{k+\ell+n+j-1}{n-j}}\delta_{k+\ell+2j}^{(n-j)}([f,g]_j(z))</math>
where <math>f</math> is a modular form of weight <math>k</math> and <math>g</math> is a modular form of weight <math>\ell</math>. Additionally, Lanphier showed that the Rankin–Cohen bracket definition can be written in terms of Maass–Shimura operators as
<math display="block">[f,g]_n=\sum_{r+s=n}(-1)^r\binom{k+n-1}{s}\binom{\ell+n-1}{r}(\delta_k^{(r)}f)(\delta_\ell^{(s)}g).</math>
